title: Teradyne Unveils Magnum E2 for the Next Wave of AI Memory
gist: Teradyne announced Magnum E2, a memory test system for LPDDR6, DDR6, GDDR7 and NAND that places instruments near the device under test to preserve signal integrity and supports NRZ, PAM3 and PAM4. The article notes no quantified yield or cost savings were provided.

insights.claim: Teradyne's Magnum E2 targets advanced DRAM and flash including LPDDR6, DDR6, GDDR7 and NAND, combining engineering and production capability on common hardware and software.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Indicates Teradyne is positioning for next-generation memory test cycles tied to AI.

insights.claim: Magnum E2 uses Near-DUT Test architecture, placing digital instruments close to the device under test to shorten the electrical path, preserve signal integrity and protect AC margin at high speeds.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Test-fixture signal loss can reduce apparent device margin, so test architecture affects yield at speed.

insights.claim: The announcement gives no quantified yield improvement or comparative measurements, so the claimed yield-at-speed benefit is an architectural objective rather than demonstrated.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Wait for customer adoption or quantified data before crediting a competitive edge.
insights.quote: However, the announcement does not provide quantified yield improvements or comparative measurements.
insights.locator: The company presents this as a way to improve yield at speed

insights.claim: The system addresses higher pin counts and greater parallelism while maintaining signal quality, balancing detailed electrical evaluation against high-volume production throughput.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Throughput per tester drives memory makers' test cost, a key economics lever.

insights.claim: Magnum E2 supports NRZ, PAM3 and PAM4 signaling and a programmable APG architecture on common hardware, intended to cover current and emerging DRAM and NAND standards without replacing the tester.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A longer-lived installed platform could improve capex payback and customer stickiness.
insights.locator: The platform supports NRZ, PAM3, and PAM4 signaling

insights.claim: Using shared hardware and software from qualification through high volume manufacturing, plus built-in logic testing to consolidate test insertions, could simplify program transfer, though the announcement does not quantify time or cost savings.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Consolidated test insertions could cut test cost, but benefits are unproven.
insights.locator: A common engineering and production platform

themes.theme: Test equipment as AI supply-chain enabler

insights.claim: Test equipment connects memory technology progress to dependable commercial output, because advanced memory creates opportunities only if manufacturers can qualify products, screen defects and sustain production economics.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Memory test is a less visible picks-and-shovels exposure to AI hardware buildouts.
insights.quote: Test equipment connects technological progress with dependable commercial output.

insights.claim: Magnum E2 is an investment in the manufacturing infrastructure behind AI rather than a new compute chip, with faster processors depending on memory systems that can supply and store data effectively.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Memory interface speed-ups create demand for new tester generations.
insights.locator: Magnum E2 therefore represents an investment
